# `•detach` — Detach

`•detach x` gives `x` with every `∂` tag removed. Under `∂`, no derivative flows back through the result, at any level of nested `∂`. Outside `∂`, `•detach x` gives `x`. Nested arrays and records are detached throughout.

```bpl
{+/⍵×⍵}∂ 1 2 3            ⍝ 2 4 6
{+/⍵×•detach ⍵}∂ 1 2 3    ⍝ 1 2 3
{⍵×•detach ⍵}∂∂ 3         ⍝ 0
```

A value computed before a `∂` call is already a constant inside it. `•detach` is needed only where the cut falls inside one call: a term that comes from the argument but must carry no gradient, such as a target built from the same parameters, or statistics treated as constants.

Apply `•detach` to a computation's inputs rather than to its result. `net •detach θ` runs `net` on plain values, at the cost of running it without `∂`, as PyTorch's `torch.no_grad()` does. `•detach net θ` runs `net` under `∂` first and then discards its derivative, as `.detach()` does. Only the first form saves the work.

A common cut falls on a shift that keeps a result finite. Logsumexp subtracts the largest item before `*` and adds it back after `⍟`. The shift drops out of the gradient. Detaching the input of `⌈/`, as here, gives the same gradient and keeps `∂` from differentiating `⌈/`:

```bpl
lse←{m←⌈/•detach ⍵ ⋄ m+⍟+/*⍵-m}
lse 1000 1001 1002        ⍝ 1002.407606
lse∂ 1 2 3                ⍝ 0.09003057317 0.2447284711 0.6652409558
```

[`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd) differentiates a function.
